scope.summary: Add a provider-neutral metering-kernel quota projection helper keyed by tenant, capability, and meter unit.
explicit_non_claims: No provider adapter, database migration, API handler, queue consumer, or production quota admission runtime is introduced.
The helper projects from an already-materialized rollup; authoritative admission still requires reserve, consume, release, concurrency control, and audit emission in an outer workflow.
No generated JSON face is hand-edited.
The ADR-0562 body mention is a source-level accounting justification for this evidence file; no firewall signoff policy or generated face is changed.
No Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, oya-ci.toml, GitHub workflow, root-hub spec, or rust-toolchain file is changed.

comparable_surfaces: AWS Service Quotas and CloudWatch usage metrics
GCP quota metrics and Service Usage control-plane admission
Azure quota usage and cost management controls
Stripe account-level metering and limit enforcement
hyperscaler_lens.provider_neutrality: The kernel uses existing Rust rollup data structures only; no AWS/GCP/Azure/Stripe SDK, database, queue, shell, Python, or CLI dependency is introduced.
hyperscaler_lens.merge_conflict_resistance: Single owned Rust source file plus one unique evidence JSON; no generated faces or shared workflow files.

facets.F1_correctness: check_quota reads the existing RollupKey total, reports used/requested/limit/remaining, allows only positive requests whose checked projected total is within limit, and denies overflow.
facets.F2_tests: Buck2 unit coverage verifies within-limit admission, over-limit denial, zero-request denial, overflow denial, and tenant/capability/unit isolation.
facets.F3_maintainability: The helper reuses RollupKey instead of introducing a duplicate quota-key abstraction.
facets.F4_compatibility: The change is additive and does not alter existing Meter, MeterEvent, rollup_window, Buck targets, Cargo manifests, or generated artifacts.
facets.F5_security: No credentials, unsafe Rust, network calls, shell execution, provider privileges, or dynamic code loading are introduced.
facets.F6_privacy: No tenant payload processing changes; only internal metering counters and public schema metadata are handled.
facets.F7_operability: QuotaDecision exposes decision fields that an outer workflow can log, meter, and audit without parsing map internals.
facets.F8_performance: Lookup is a single BTreeMap get against an already-materialized rollup; no unbounded scan is added to the quota check.
facets.F9_compliance: No hand-edited *.generated.json files and no new dependencies. New public fields carry inline data_class annotations.
facets.F10_reversibility: Rollback is a normal git revert of one Rust contract file and this evidence file; no data migration or production state mutation is introduced.
facets.F11_observability: Decision output is explicit enough for future metrics and audit emission, while this slice avoids claiming runtime instrumentation.
facets.F13_migration: Moves billing toward owned-stack quota/capacity enforcement by adding the provider-neutral kernel projection before adapters or API handlers.

fixed_findings: Added direct capability and unit isolation assertions.
Documented check_quota as snapshot projection, not authoritative quota admission.
